title: How to get reverse dependencies in Debian package manager for installed packages
body:
The typical way to get reverse dependencies in Debian or Debian based systems, is to either use

apt-cache rdepends PackageName

OR

apt-cache showpkg PackageName

There are two issues with this. Firstly it lists all the reverse dependencies of a package, regardless of whether the dependency is Depends, Suggests, Recommends. Secondly it does not check if the dependent package is already installed or not on the system.

For example let us consider the package graphviz. Looking at its reverse dependencies we can see that there are packages like gimp and qvge(i.e. Qt Visual Graph Editor) which depend on graphviz. i.e. without graphviz installed on the system these cannot work. However there are also packages which only suggest or recommends graphviz to be installed like travis (i.e. trajectory analyzer and visualizer), webdruid and others. These packages do not require graphviz to be installed. Rather they will function just fine without graphviz.

So how is it possible to find the reverse dependencies of a package in which the type of dependency is "Depends", not Suggests nor Recommends and also to list only those packages which are installed? Taking the above example how is it possible to list only gimp, qvge, plus other packages for graphviz while omit packages like travis and webdruid?

title: How to analyze output of systemd dependency graph
body:
What is the correct method to analyze the dependency graph produced by systemd-analyze dot ?

I want all journal logs, so /var/log to be stored persistently on a separate partition and make / read only. But I run into the situation that systemd tries to mount before the mmc device is ready, and the mount service times out. I have described that issue in more detail in this post.

I wanted to test if I could somehow add a service just to delay the start of journaling, allowing udev and mmc devices more time to settle. For that I need to know the order in which services are started by systemd.

To get the dependency graph I did:

systemd-analyze dot > depend.dot
dot -Tsvg depend.dot -o depend.svg

I converted the dot file to a svg but the resulting graphic is very complicated.

What is the best way to analyze such a graph? Is there a better way to convert the dot file for a better visualization? I am mainly interested in a way to analyze the order in which services are started.
